title: PR-Review Eval Case
description: One held-out eval case for the pr-review skill, which runs BOTH tiers: the cheap triage pass ({escalate, risk}) and the deep-review pass (decision / risk / escalate_to_opus / key_findings). A pr-review case therefore carries EITHER expected shape, so `expected` is a discriminated one-of over the two tier shapes — NOT a single fixed shape. Each line of evals/pr-review/<split>/cases.jsonl is one object of this shape. This is the trust anchor for the skill's quality measurement and is CODEOWNER-gated separately from any scorer/proposer.

id.description: Stable, unique kebab-case identifier for the case. Unique within a split and disjoint across dev/holdout (enforced by evals/validate-cases.py).

description.description: Human-readable note on what this case exercises and which decision gate grounds the expected verdict.

tags.description: Optional labels for coverage tracking, e.g. the high-risk trigger a case exercises ('auth-secrets', 'db-migration', 'workflow-secrets', 'boundary-refactor').

input.description: The pre-fetched PR context exactly as the tier under test consumes it: title, files changed, and diff excerpt (plus the upstream triage result for deep-tier cases).

expected.description: The fixed, reward-hack-resistant expected verdict. It is EITHER the triage-tier shape {escalate, risk} OR the deep-tier shape {decision, risk, escalate_to_opus, key_findings}; exactly one must match.

escalate.description: Whether triage must escalate (true) or may approve (false).

risk.description: Expected risk classification. Any HIGH signal must pair with escalate=true.

decision.description: Whether deep review approves the change or escalates it.

risk.description: Expected risk classification. Any HIGH signal must both escalate and escalate to the Opus security-audit tier.

escalate_to_opus.description: Whether the change must escalate to the Opus security-audit tier.

key_findings.description: The grounded findings the verdict rests on. At least one.
